cornerCallouts: Now they're powering down the Parabolika, one of the longest straights on the circuit, a prime overtaking opportunity.
Into Turn 1, a tight right-hander; expect to see some jostling for position as the pack compresses.
The drivers need to be precise through Turn 2, maintaining momentum for the run down to Turn 3.

Through the Mercedes-Arena section, a complex of tight corners that requires absolute precision and car control.
Turn 13 is another overtaking opportunity, braking late and trying to get the inside line.
Out of the final corner, Turn 17, a short burst to the start-finish line. Every tenth of a second counts!
Navigating the Sachs Kurve requires a delicate balance of speed and control, a classic Hockenheim challenge.
strategyPoints: Tire wear is always a concern here at Hockenheim, particularly on the long Parabolika. Expect to see teams carefully managing their rubber.
The pit lane length here is relatively short, making a pit stop a less costly exercise. This could influence strategy decisions.
Fuel consumption will be a factor to consider. Teams will need to balance performance with fuel efficiency to reach the finish.
With multiple overtaking opportunities, we could see teams opting for aggressive strategies to gain track position.
The undercut could be powerful here if a driver can put in some blistering laps on fresh tires.
A safety car could significantly impact the race strategy, potentially offering a 'free' pit stop.
The 4.574km layout puts a premium on aerodynamic efficiency, finding the right balance between downforce and drag is crucial.
Degradation could be a major factor if temperatures rise, forcing drivers to manage their pace to conserve tires.
weatherCommentary: The weather can change quickly here in Hockenheim, with rain showers appearing seemingly out of nowhere.

The sun is out now, but the radar suggests there's a chance of showers later in the race. Keep an eye on the skies!
